commit.message: fix(pending): reconcile applied proposals without replay (MAGI-004)

specification.objective: MAGI-004: guard pending records that may have been applied even if cleanup failed or a process terminated. Offer conservative recovery and avoid any automatic replay or claims of exactly-once.

requirements.statement: After successful native memory apply, cleanup failure returns applied_cleanup_failed; block repeat approval during same process/session.
Persist minimal content-free Magi-owned reconciliation marker outside pending/memory to recognize the same proposal after restart; use profile-specific scope.
If a pending add already exists in store but no marker proves why, show ambiguous and refuse approval; allow explicit reject without automatically modifying stored content.
UI communicates reconciliation and does not offer automatic retry; handle marker persistence errors conservatively and document non-atomic crash windows.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Simulated successful apply then failed unlink cannot invoke native apply again, including fresh API module reload for same profile.
Stored-memory equivalence without marker yields ambiguous status for add, and reject remains accessible.
Marker contains no raw memory and is profile scoped; successful cleanup does not leave lingering marker.
Regressions, verify.sh, POLIS gates pass with honest recovery documentation.

invariants.statement: Memory persistence delegated to Hermes public APIs only; Magi-owned metadata outside Hermes pending/memory queue.
Approval remains explicit and no guarantee of exactly-once or rollback.

forbidden_states.statement: Automatic repeat approval after known applied_cleanup_failed.
Marker stores memory content, tokens, prompt text, or edits Hermes queue structure.

inputs.statement: TASKS.md MAGI-004 and MAGI-002 applied_cleanup_failed response.

outputs.statement: Magi-owned reconciliation journal, guarded approval, status/UI feedback and regressions.

failure_semantics.statement: Unknown crash state remains ambiguous; manual review/rejection required; no atomic two-system transaction.
